blocks.content: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 bestowed constitutional status upon rural and urban local bodies in India, establishing grassroots democracy.

rows: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation

items: Panchayats deal with 29 functional items in the 11th Schedule, whereas Municipalities deal with 18 functional items in the 12th Schedule.
Articles 243 to 243O cover Panchayats, while Articles 243P to 243ZG cover Municipalities.
State Finance Commission is constituted every 5 years under Article 243-I (Panchayats) and Article 243-Y (Municipalities) to review financial position.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Panchayats govern rural local areas under Part IX (11th Schedule, 29 functional items), while Municipalities govern urban local areas under Part IXA (12th Schedule, 18 functional items).
Both the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 conferred constitutional status on local self-government institutions in India.
Both systems mandate a 3-tier structure in larger states and require a minimum age of 21 years to contest elections.
Not less than one-third (1/3rd) of total seats are reserved for women in both rural and urban local bodies.
State Election Commission conducts elections every 5 years for both Panchayats and Municipalities.
